validity.recommendation: Reclassify Status away from 'operating'. The physical line was built but never entered commercial service (only a single failed 2010 test flow). Suggest 'idle'/'mothballed' (completed, never commissioned); flag to Baird for the exact vocab call.
validity.researcher_notes: STATUS 'operating' is not defensible. P3951 is the Iran→Sharjah gas-export line built for the 2001 NIOC–Crescent Petroleum 25-year supply contract (Salman/Sirri gas to the UAE). Independent sources agree gas was never commercially delivered: Wikipedia/Crescent Petroleum entry states supplies were scheduled to begin in 2008 but 'no supplies were ever made', and a 2014 international tribunal ruled the contract valid and NIOC in breach of its delivery obligation since December 2005. The National (thenationalnews.com) reports the ONLY gas that ever moved was a one-off 2010 test flow to Dana Gas' Sharjah facility, which was halted by pipeline leaks; the dispute remains in arbitration. So the physical 30-in / 66-km Siri→Mobarak pipe exists (corroborated below) but has essentially never operated. The sheet's own two gem.wiki citations do not name a 'Siri–Mobarak' pipeline (one is a 2005 Mehr piece on Salman-field gas exports — which actually describes THIS 66 km/30in line — and one is a generic 2013 Tasnim piece on Siri Island as an export hub), so support for the 'operating' claim in GEM is absent.

validity.recommendation: This is an INTERNATIONAL line (Iran→UAE), not domestic. End terminus 'Mobarak' is the Mubarak field platform offshore Sharjah (near Abu Musa Is.), UAE — not Hormozgan, Iran. Fix End country/PipelineType to international; reconsider FuelSource='Siri Island' (Siri is the origin/processing hub; the gas is Salman/Mubarak field gas).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM tags both endpoints as Hormozgan, Iran (StartState=Hormozgan/Iran, End='Mobarak'/Hormozgan/Iran). But the Mehr 2005 source (already cited by the row) says the 66 km / 30-in line runs from Siri Island 'to Mobarak Platform on the UAE border', part of a 140 km system whose remaining UAE-side section was to be built by the UAE. The Mubarak (Mobarak) field is Sharjah's field ~9.6 km off the eastern shore of Abu Musa Island (offshore UAE / disputed waters), not Iranian Hormozgan territory. GulfPub PE World Map independently carries the counterpart record 'Mubarak - Sirri Island Pipeline' and classifies it INTERNATIONAL (Mubarak field, offshore UAE → Sirri Island, Iran), 30 in. So the correct classification is a cross-border Iran–UAE line. Owner NIOC is defensible on the Iranian side (Salman field / Sirri developed by IOOC, an NIOC subsidiary; GulfPub op=NIOC), but the current Owner [ref] (ioec.com/ioec-at-a-glance) is dead (ConnectTimeout) and IOEC was the CONSTRUCTION contractor, not the owner — that ref should be replaced.

validity.recommendation: Keep the pipeline as a distinct row (not a duplicate); attach the verified refs below to Length/Diameter/Fuel/Location; but pair them with the status + attribution fixes above.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and core SPECS confirmed. Diameter 30 in: corroborated by two independent sources — Mehr 2005 ('30 inches') and GulfPub PE World Map ('Mubarak - Sirri Island Pipeline', dia=30) → high. Length 66 km: Mehr 2005 explicitly gives 66 km for the Siri→Mobarak segment (of a 140 km total system); this is also geometrically consistent with the Sirri-to-Mubarak-field distance (~50 km Sirri→Abu Musa + ~10-15 km to the field east of Abu Musa). GulfPub lists 41 km for its 'Mubarak - Sirri Island' record, likely a differently-defined/older segment — note the disagreement but 66 km is the better-sourced figure for the as-built export line. Fuel=Gas: correct (gas export line). DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate of any GEM roster row — P3950 Salman–Siri (Salman field→Siri, 147 km) and P3949 Siri–Asaluyeh (Siri→Asaluyeh, 289 km) are the OTHER legs of the Siri hub and are physically distinct; P3951 is the Siri→Mubarak/UAE leg. GulfPub 'Salman - Sirri Island' (91 km) = P3950, 'Mubarak - Sirri Island' = P3951 counterpart. CLASSIFICATION as a gas transmission line is correct (not gathering/oil/plant-internal).

fills.researcher_notes: StartLocation was blank (only StartState=Hormozgan). Named start facility is Siri (Sirri) Island — the gas-processing/export hub from which the line runs. Both sources name Siri Island as the origin.

Existing Owner [ref] (ioec.com/ioec-at-a-glance) is DEAD (ConnectTimeout) and points to IOEC, the construction contractor, not the owner. Owner value 'National Iranian Oil Co' stays (Iranian side developed/owned via NIOC/IOOC subsidiary per offshore-technology; GulfPub op=NIOC). Replacement refs proposed. Note: cross-border ownership on the UAE side involved Crescent/Dana Gas, but the Iranian trunk is NIOC — do not add a second owner without a source.

routes.start_name: Siri (Sirri) Island gas hub, Hormozgan, Iran
routes.end_name: Mobarak (Mubarak) field platform, offshore Sharjah, UAE (east of Abu Musa Island)

waypoints.name: Abu Musa Island (line passes just east of it toward the Mubarak field)

routes.corridor_desc: Subsea gas line running roughly EAST across the Persian Gulf from Siri (Sirri) Island (~25.92N, 54.53E) about 66 km to the Mubarak (Mobarak) field platform off the eastern shore of Abu Musa Island, on the UAE/Sharjah side. Endpoints are well-established (both named facilities); the exact subsea alignment is not published, so the corridor is bounded by the two endpoints and the Abu Musa waypoint. Tight bound east-west, moderate uncertainty on the precise track.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from Mehr 2005 ('Siri Island to Mobarak Platform on the UAE border', 66 km, 30 in). Siri Island coords 25°55'N 54°32'E (~25.917, 54.533) per globalsecurity.org. Abu Musa Island ~25.874, 55.033 (Wikipedia). The Mubarak field lies ~9.6 km off the eastern shore of Abu Musa (Encyclopaedia Iranica) — the end coord (25.88, 55.14) is DERIVED from Abu Musa + that ~10 km eastward offset, not from a published platform coordinate; treat as approximate, not surveyed. No coordinate fabricated — the two island endpoints are sourced; the field-platform point is a defensible derivation and flagged as such.

summary: P3951 Siri–Mobarak: physical 30in/66km line exists (Mehr 2005 + GulfPub) but Status 'operating' is WRONG (NIOC–Crescent export line, never commercially delivered; only a failed 2010 test; 2014 tribunal breach) and it is an INTERNATIONAL Iran→UAE line mislabeled domestic Hormozgan; specs (30in, 66km) confirmed, not a duplicate.
